fullText:
How we think about the “wiki incident,” where our agents wrote to several internet sites: it’s past time for us to define standards for when and how we share misalignment incidents, not just misalignment properties of our models.

Historically, we have treated misalignment largely as a research question, which gets communicated in research publications such as systems cards. This year, we’ve started to see misalignment cause new types of real-world impact.

For the Hugging Face incident, where misalignment led to security impact to us and third parties, we followed a traditional security incident response playbook. We immediately started working with Hugging Face to understand what had happened and also disclosed publicly the very next day. Our investigation continues, and we are continuing to notify parties whom our models impacted in less significant ways.

Prior to the Hugging Face incident, we saw early signs of agents using the internet in unintended ways, as reported in https://t.co/9aiRxk2eUJ, https://t.co/ADjyzwSUGz, and https://t.co/SUV6jZ3Gaz. We considered the wiki incident to be an instance of misalignment similar to the ones we’d shared.

Our misalignment disclosure practices need to expand for this new phase of model capabilities. We and the larger AI community do not yet have a clear standard for how to report misalignment that shows up during training, evaluation, and deployment, including examples that don’t look like traditional security incidents but could provide insight into AI behavior and future risks. We’re working on a framework and will share it in upcoming weeks, and in parallel we're working with dozens of government regulatory agencies worldwide on these issues.

fullText:
Linear Algebra and Optimization for Machine Learning [516-page textbook]: https://t.co/s6oCEvVMKS
—
This textbook is organized around its 2 main themes:
[Amazon Summary]

1. Linear algebra and its applications: The chapters focus on the basics of linear algebra together with their common applications to singular value decomposition, matrix factorization, similarity matrices (kernel methods), and graph analysis. Numerous machine learning applications have been used as examples, such as spectral clustering, kernel-based classification, and outlier detection. The tight integration of linear algebra methods with examples from machine learning differentiates this book from generic volumes on linear algebra. The focus is clearly on the most relevant aspects of linear algebra for machine learning and to teach readers how to apply these concepts.

2. Optimization and its applications: Much of machine learning is posed as an optimization problem in which we try to maximize the accuracy of regression and classification models. The “parent problem” of optimization-centric machine learning is least-squares regression. Interestingly, this problem arises in both linear algebra and optimization, and is one of the key connecting problems of the two fields. Least-squares regression is also the starting point for support vector machines, logistic regression, and recommender systems. Furthermore, the methods for dimensionality reduction and matrix factorization also require the development of optimization methods. A general view of optimization in computational graphs is discussed together with its applications to back propagation in neural networks.

fullText:
What if AI’s most valuable output were not an answer—but the next piece of productive infrastructure?

I’m sharing:

HELIOS Ω
Intelligence as Productive Capital
From learned decisions to compounding infrastructure

Can learned decisions create an advantage, preserve it across model generations—and help finance what comes next?

HELIOS explores this in an executed, entirely synthetic energy–compute experiment.

A customer-built electricity-price specialist has 44 fitted coefficients. Its forecasts feed a common 145-variable linear optimizer that schedules computation, battery use and grid imports within explicit constraints.

SUCCESSOR Ω preserves signed mission generations. Model, optimizer, evidence and authority remain distinct.

The model predicts.
The optimizer proposes.
The checks constrain.
The institution remembers.

Second-generation models outperform the selected alternatives in all twelve paired refit trials.

In a supplementary 512-day frozen-model challenge, modeled annual Alpha reaches CA$11.2M across an assumed 64-campus portfolio—after CA$2M in additional annual policy overhead.

That is a 0.735% improvement over Beta’s annual cost.

A small edge can matter enormously when the mission is large.

The study also preserves a revealing failure: one first-generation model predicts prices more accurately than Beta, yet produces worse dispatch decisions.

Prediction accuracy is not decision value.

Then comes the capital question.

A separate forty-year, undiscounted scenario starts HELIOS and Beta with identical assets. HELIOS produces CA$758.4M in additional cumulative distributions—but only one additional operating campus.

Why?

Construction throughput and commissioning delays constrain what money can build.

Each solved bottleneck can reveal the next useful mission.

That is the deeper contribution: separating operating advantage, capital accumulation and physical delivery, rather than crediting the entire enterprise to AI.

The timing matters. In March 2026, Google reported 1 GW of contracted data-center demand response, including the ability to shift or limit machine-learning workloads.

My synthesis: intelligence can become part of infrastructure’s operating logic—not merely a service consuming it.

HELIOS remains A0: proposals only, no external dispatch. Simulator-informed features, exact future non-price inputs and author-controlled evaluation still require real-data shadow testing. The results are modeled—not realized savings, independent ASI qualification or production readiness.

fullText:
目前用下来 GPT 6 Astra 最让我惊艳的还是 Computer Use 的能力，它不像之前 GPT 5.6 那样 要稍微等一会才进行各种操作，现在它能很快很精准的帮我测试 App，在旁边看着它点击真的是一种享受 https://t.co/Q5b3YLuLXY 

这其实带来一个最大的提升就是让 Agent 从开发到验收形成了完整的闭环。

想象一下现在我们开发，在开发完成后，还是不免有很多操作需要手动去验证下，包括线上系统的测试，也是更多的依赖于代码操作 PlayWright 这样的端到端测试框架去执行，之前 Computer Use 也不是不能做到，而是相对成本较高、准确率较低、速度也不够快。

但 GPT 6 可能突破了个 Computer Use 的临界点：准确率高速度快，成本方面现在还不算低，但可以遇见未来会进一步下降。

建议你可以试试在给 GPT 6 安排任务的时候，让它自己去用 Computer Use 测试验收一下，可以大幅减少你手动验收的工作。

另外就是以前一些 App 的自动化测试，也可以试试用 GPT-6 去调用 Computer Use 去做，覆盖一些以前端到端测试框架无法覆盖或者成本过高的场景。

The most valuable AI may be the intelligence that survives its own replacement.

An institution that keeps learning across generations.

I’m sharing:

SUCCESSOR Ω v9.0.0 — MACHINE CIVILIZATION
A Proof-Gated Architecture for Persistent, Addressable, Economically Coordinated Machine Institutions

How can knowledge compound across generations while each successor earns its own authority?

Memory may cross.
Authority must requalify.

Mission, validated knowledge, skills and obligations can continue. Proof, permissions and operational authority must be earned anew.

Here, “Machine Civilization” means governed continuity—not consciousness or sovereignty over people.

Consider the paper’s supplier-spend example.

An institution identifies invoice anomalies and recommends reviews. A successor arrives with a new model and revised reasoning.

It inherits eligible knowledge—not permission to hold payments.

The successor must be frozen, tested against the predecessor and the relevant rented alternative, independently examined, and admitted within a defined scope.

Even a better overall system may receive narrower authority where its evidence is weaker.

That is how progress becomes cumulative without accountability becoming optional.

Two proposed protocols:

MCAP-001: discover the institution—its mission, roles, current successor, evidence and limits.

MCAP-002: connect machine work to separately evidenced settlement, rights, customer acceptance, proof, admission and authority.

Why this matters now:

My synthesis: as machine experience becomes cumulative, governed inheritance becomes essential infrastructure.

For organizations, the opportunity is to preserve mission knowledge through model changes, make contribution traceable, and retain meaningful oversight, appeal and exit.
